## Summary

The change rejects creating an owner whose lower-cased email already belongs to another owner, returning **409 Conflict**.

Owner creation lives only in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`, which already delegates each business rule to a small, single-purpose helper class in the `v1` package (`CityCapacity`, `HouseholdDuplicates`, etc.) and folds them into one conflict-returning condition. I followed that exact pattern to keep structural impact minimal:

1. **New file** `rest/controller/v1/DuplicateEmails.java` — a small, cohesive helper (mirroring `CityCapacity`) with one static `isTaken(candidate, existing)` method. Comparison is case-insensitive (`equalsIgnoreCase`, i.e. lower-cased) and null candidate emails are never treated as duplicates. Its surrounding class complexity is ~0, so the bulk of the new logic pays almost nothing.

2. **One-line edit** in `OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner` — added `|| DuplicateEmails.isTaken(owner, existingOwners)` to the existing `if (... ) return CONFLICT;` condition, reusing the already-loaded `existingOwners` collection.

Only the single conflict predicate in the large controller class was touched (one added term), keeping the expensive WMC_other-weighted cost to a minimum; all the real behaviour sits in the new zero-context helper.
